orientation: A reproducible synthetic-audio rerun repaired the provenance and transcript-fidelity problems of an earlier study, and both preregistered gates passed. Matched cues still showed no advantage over shuffled cues on automatic response proxies, leaving the result negative/inconclusive until human conversational-quality review exists.
finding: The apparatus and provenance repair succeeded, but automatic diagnostics did not show that correctly matched neutral-synthesis cues help more than shuffled cues.
limitations: The downstream model changed from the unavailable historical model to a preregistered successor.
The diagnostics measure behavior change rather than empathy or conversational quality.
External text and generated artifacts remain outside source control because the dataset license is undisclosed.
negative_evidence: Matched cues were not uniquely closer to text-only responses than shuffled cues.
No proxy demonstrated a matched-cue advantage, and human quality review was not performed.
evidence_quotes: The provenance repair succeeded: this run has exact text/audio fidelity, immutable audio hashes, a known synthesizer, and genuinely distinct matched/shuffled cue blocks.
The automatic downstream result nevertheless remains negative/inconclusive.
Nothing in these proxies demonstrates that correctly matched neutral-synthesis cues help more than shuffled cues.
Human review would be required for a conversational-quality claim, but the prior result no longer depends on unknowable third-party audio generation.
